rationale: Check if the strict butterfly-family x botanical-family host identity effect (p=0.030) is dominated by a single common host plant family.
selection: The eight most linked botanical families selected using frozen HOSTS interactions alone, before any botanical family LOO results
statistic: Same original climate-analogue-minus-discordant difference in contemporary-minus-native regional butterfly-resource Jaccard, with one complete botanical family of host links excluded from observed AND randomized networks.
null: Double-edge swaps within butterfly-family x botanical-family link classes in the full network, preserving host degree and butterfly plant-family diet composition. Exclusion is only in evaluation, not in the swap process.
climate_groups: Pre-frozen four-BIO distances, 12,944 far cross-Level1 climate analog and 12,944 discordant regional pairs
decision: All-positive LOO excess supports direction robustness but NOT an independent butterfly mechanism; sign reversals expose single-family dependence. Treat all p values as descriptive posthoc audits; do not select favorable subsets.
boundaries: Output remains potential larval-resource geography, not realized butterfly response or fitness.
If a butterfly loses all host links after deleting one plant family, retain it as an empty resource species in the same frozen 239-butterfly frame.
p-values generated from network randomizations, not independence of regional pairs.
No changes to the GEB main manuscript.
